title: Forest’s Morgan Gibbs-White avoids concussion after head injury vs. Chelsea, says Vitor Pereira
content:
Vitor Pereira believes that Morgan Gibbs-White does not have a concussion, following the injury he sustained in Nottingham Forest’s 3-1 win at Chelsea.

Forest’s talisman was forced off with a head injury barely 20 minutes after being introduced as a half-time substitute at Stamford Bridge. His importance to the side was underlined as he set up Taiwo Awoniyi to score Forest’s third goal, before he was involved with a nasty clash of heads with Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sanchez.

But while the moment ended his participation in the capital, Pereira is hopeful that the attacking midfielder will be available to face Aston Villa in the Europa League semi-final second leg on Thursday night.

“No, no, no. I think no. I had a conversation with him and he was speaking normally; he remembers everything. The only thing is to look after his face and the pain of his injury. We will see,” said Pereira, when asked in his press conference if he feared Gibbs-White might have a concussion.

“I am waiting. I am not a doctor. Gibbs-White has a deep cut (just above the bridge of his nose). But he is a fighter. He has a strong mentality. I hope our medical team can do magic to put him in the right condition.

“I have told him he does not need to head the ball, he only needs to play … We will see.”

If Gibbs-White was to enter the concussion protocol, his participation in the second leg would have been in doubt. The FA’s concussion guidelines state that the earliest a player can return to play is seven days after the incident, providing that the exceptional criteria is met.

Pereira made eight changes to his Forest side with one eye on that game, with Forest holding a 1-0 aggregate lead from the first leg, with Chris Wood, Elliot Anderson, Gibbs-White, Neco Williams, Omari Hutchinson and Nikola Milenkovic all moved to the bench.

Two goals from Taiwo Awoniyi and another from Igor Jesus helped Forest to three points that left them six points clear of 18th-placed West Ham United, with a vastly superior goal difference.

Pereira believes defender Zach Abbott should be fit to play, after he was also forced off with a head injury in the first half.

“Zach, I spoke to him in the dressing room and he will be okay,” said Pereira, who was impressed by the spirit of his side.

“We are without Callum (Hudson-Odoi), we are without Dan (Ndoye) — two of our wingers. We are without Murillo and, before today, without Jair Cunha. He has a shoulder problem but he is a fighter. We are without Sangare. We are without Ola (Aina).

“It was not difficult for me to pick my starting XI because, when you do not have many solutions, I do not need to think a lot.

“In the end, we are doing well, because of the spirit we have. Even without the important players, we keep our spirit. This is not a tactical thing, it is about the spirit of the team.”
